regulator-vacuum-line.summary: The regulator references intake manifold pressure through a vacuum hose. This lets it regulate the pressure difference across the injectors rather than fuel pressure relative to outside air alone.
regulator-vacuum-line.limits: Ford confirms the vacuum connection. The dedicated plenum fitting, hose route, dimensions and sealing geometry are assumptions; the actual truck may route this through a shared vacuum harness. No pressure or leak-rate simulation is implemented.

steps.title: Communicate manifold pressure
steps.text: An open plenum port and fitting lead into the hose. The modeled port is an illustrative location, not a production drilling specification.

steps.title: Reference the diaphragm chamber
steps.text: The hose fits around the regulator nipple and reaches the spring side of the diaphragm. This connection is distinct from the fuel supply and return passages.

induction.summary: The EFI intake is built from two castings. Air passes from the throttle interface into a shared plenum, through six curved runners, and down to the cylinder-head intake ports.
induction.limits: This is a layout reconstruction. Factory references support component identities and architecture. Runner shapes, mounting dimensions and installed positions remain provisional. Wiring, vacuum hoses, tank-side fuel hoses and EGR remain incomplete.

steps.title: Shared plenum and long runners
steps.text: The upper casting distributes incoming air among the six passages. Use Cutaway to inspect its hollow plenum and runner bores. These passages belong to a single casting.

steps.title: Lower manifold
steps.text: The lower casting turns air toward the head. Six separate injector assemblies fit into modeled sockets at this end of the intake. Socket and port profiles are provisional.

steps.title: A sealed joint
steps.text: A separate gasket seals the upper-to-lower joint. Seven retaining studs hold the castings together; their count comes from the truck service procedure.

troubleshooting.title: Leaks at a sealing joint
troubleshooting.text: The gasket interfaces must seal the intake air path. A damaged gasket or poorly seated joint can admit unwanted air. The model identifies those interfaces; it does not perform a vacuum-leak diagnosis.

troubleshooting.title: Missing connections matter
troubleshooting.text: The wiring, vacuum hoses, PCV and EGR connections are part of the installed system. Their current absence is a modeling gap.

throttle-assembly.summary: Two butterfly plates share a shaft. Moving the throttle-opening slider turns them together, changing how much of each bore is obstructed.
throttle-assembly.limits: Factory references support twin bores, a separate gasket, four mounting studs/nuts, an IAC valve and a TPS. Dimensions and internal packaging remain provisional. Linkage, return spring, bracket, plate screws, IAC fasteners and harness are still missing.

steps.title: Air passages
steps.text: The twin bores lead into the shared upper plenum. Use See through covers to watch the plates inside.

steps.title: Paired plates
steps.text: A common shaft coordinates the two discs. At 90 degrees the idealized discs are edge-on to the incoming air. Production closed and full-open stops still need verification.

steps.title: Idle uses another path
steps.text: The IAC-controlled bypass is a separate passage around the plates. The model now includes two passages and an unvented IAC study; the installed valve variant is unverified.

troubleshooting.title: Separate throttle opening from idle control
troubleshooting.text: Closed butterfly plates do not mean the real engine has no air supply: the IAC meters a separate bypass path. The viewer does not simulate idle speed or air flow.

troubleshooting.title: Sealing interface
troubleshooting.text: The separate gasket seals the body to the upper manifold. Inspect its position in the exploded view.

fuel-system.summary: The supply rail feeds six solenoid-operated injectors. Each injector meters fuel by opening for a controlled time. The vacuum-referenced regulator returns excess fuel toward the tank.
fuel-system.limits: Source diagrams establish the architecture and internal component identities. All geometry and installed stations are provisional. Rail supports, spring-lock couplings, pressure-test valve, wiring, vacuum hose and calibrated fuel paths remain incomplete.

steps.title: Shared supply
steps.text: A hollow rail feeds six injector cups. The separate return tube connects the regulator outlet toward the tank.

steps.title: Inside one injector
steps.text: Explore the coil, armature, needle, spring, inlet filter, body and seals. Pulse duration meters fuel; this model does not predict flow or spray.

steps.title: Pressure balance
steps.text: The diaphragm senses fuel pressure on one side and manifold pressure plus spring load on the other. The return valve opens to bypass excess fuel.

troubleshooting.title: Distinguish the seals
troubleshooting.text: Each injector has an upper rail seal and a lower manifold seal. The model keeps their identities separate. Fuel-pressure testing and service require the applicable factory procedure.

troubleshooting.title: Do not infer flow from a visible opening
troubleshooting.text: Actual injector calibration depends on pressure, pulse duration and nozzle geometry. These study dimensions are not flow specifications.

idle-air.summary: The IAC solenoid moves a reverse-seated pintle to meter air through a path around the throttle plates. The controller uses it to manage idle and changing loads.
idle-air.limits: The manual illustrates unvented and vent/filter variants. This is an unvented teaching study, with unverified installed applicability, dimensions and routing. It has no pressure, duty-cycle or idle-speed simulation.

steps.title: Independent bypass
steps.text: Two openings connect the upstream and downstream sides of the throttle to the valve chamber.

steps.title: Electromagnetic actuator
steps.text: The coil acts on the armature, which moves the pintle and changes the bypass opening.

troubleshooting.title: Identify the variant first
troubleshooting.text: The factory text gives different serviceability for the two illustrated valve types. Do not infer that the installed valve can be cleaned from this model.

throttle-sensor.summary: The TPS is a rotary potentiometer. A wiper turns with the throttle shaft over a curved resistance track, producing the throttle-position signal.
throttle-sensor.limits: The track and wiper illustrate the factory operating description. Their dimensions, packaging and angular/voltage calibration are unverified. No electrical diagnostic simulation is provided.

steps.title: Turn the shaft
steps.text: Use Throttle opening and See through covers to watch the sensor rotor and wiper move together.

steps.title: Stationary track
steps.text: The resistance track remains fixed while the wiper moves. Three electrical circuits connect reference, return and signal; harness details remain missing.

troubleshooting.title: Mechanical and electrical faults differ
troubleshooting.text: A freely moving throttle can still have a sensor or wiring problem. The geometric animation does not validate the electrical signal.

exhaust.summary: Separate front and rear castings collect exhaust from three cylinders each. The passages merge into two outlets.
exhaust.limits: Manufacturer references support the split castings and rounded-rectangular entry shapes. Both entry sets, the front collector, a three-part lifting-eye mounting study and a provisional EGR fitting/tube joint are represented. Port dimensions, casting identity, wall thickness, installed positions and EGR routing remain unverified. The rear collector contour, remaining manifold fasteners, air-injection hardware and exhaust-pipe joints are unfinished.

steps.title: Front three cylinders
steps.text: The front casting combines three head ports into one collector.

steps.title: Rear three cylinders
steps.text: The rear casting serves the other three cylinders. Its production EGR connection remains to be modeled.

troubleshooting.title: Use the correct joint instructions
troubleshooting.text: The factory procedure distinguishes exhaust-manifold installation from the intake gasket. Do not add a generic combined gasket based on this study.

fuel-test-valve.summary: The rail diagnostic fitting provides access for a fuel-pressure tester. Its spring-loaded core normally closes the passage.
fuel-test-valve.limits: Ford confirms the diagnostic fitting; internal geometry is a generic valve study. Exact part identity, materials, threads and installed location remain unverified.

steps.title: Fuel reaches the fitting
steps.text: A branch bore connects the test fitting to the rail supply passage.

steps.title: The pin opens the seated valve
steps.text: Depressing the actuating pin moves the soft seat off its mating surface. The spring returns it toward closure; the external sleeve seals around the cartridge.

steps.title: The cap closes the outer boundary
steps.text: The cap helps seal the fitting and keeps debris away from the exposed port.

troubleshooting.title: Compare pressure using the applicable test
troubleshooting.text: Ford lists 50–60 psi key-on/engine-off and 45–60 psi at idle for this application. Follow the linked precautions and test procedure; this model does not simulate pressure or diagnose a leak.

fuel-rail-assembly.summary: The supply and return tubes connect the injectors and regulator. Three fasteners retain the rail on the lower intake; the test valve provides diagnostic access.
fuel-rail-assembly.limits: Bolt diameter, pitch and under-head length follow the Ford exploded drawing. Rail bends, casting bosses, bolt-head/washer shapes, station coordinates and female threads remain provisional.

steps.title: Three mounts retain the rail
steps.text: Ford shows three 1/4-20 × .90-inch bolts with washers. The model keeps each fastener separate and provides matching support bosses and bores on the lower intake.

steps.title: The cups seal around the injectors
steps.text: Injector O-rings seal the fuel connections. The service procedure installs injectors into the rail before fitting the assembly to the lower intake.

troubleshooting.title: A disturbed rail needs a seal and mounting check
troubleshooting.text: Use the linked factory procedure for O-ring handling, coupling engagement and retaining-fastener tightening. Provisional CAD clearances do not establish leak-tight assembly.

fuel-supply-coupling.summary: Two seals prevent leakage; a garter spring captures the female flare; an external clip adds redundant retention.
fuel-supply-coupling.limits: Documented construction with provisional dimensions and rail stations. No pressure, sealing, spring-force or installed fit validation. Tank-side hose routing is not modeled.

steps.title: A sealed sliding connection
steps.text: The female socket slides over two O-rings carried by the male spigot. Explode the assembly to distinguish the two seals.

steps.title: Spring and cage retain the flare
steps.text: The coiled garter spring sits inside the male cage. After the female flare passes it, the spring contracts behind the flare.

steps.title: Redundant safety clip
steps.text: Ford specifies a large black supply clip and a small gray return clip. The tether keeps it associated with the line.

troubleshooting.title: Connection does not lock
troubleshooting.text: Ford calls for checking that the female flare is captured behind the spring and verifying engagement by pulling the connection. The viewer does not simulate insertion or retention force.

troubleshooting.title: Seal condition and identity
troubleshooting.text: The factory procedure calls for two specified fuel-resistant O-rings. Similar-looking generic seals do not establish a correct replacement.

fuel-return-coupling.summary: Two seals prevent leakage; a garter spring captures the female flare; an external clip adds redundant retention.
fuel-return-coupling.limits: Documented construction with provisional dimensions and rail stations. No pressure, sealing, spring-force or installed fit validation. Tank-side hose routing is not modeled.

steps.text: The female socket slides over two O-rings carried by the male spigot. Explode the assembly to distinguish the two seals.

steps.title: Spring and cage retain the flare
steps.text: The coiled garter spring sits inside the male cage. After the female flare passes it, the spring contracts behind the flare.

pcv-valve-assembly.summary: Crankcase ventilation returns blow-by gases to the intake. A spring-loaded plunger meters flow, and a separate grommet locates the valve in the cover.
pcv-valve-assembly.limits: Factory mechanism and replacement-photo exterior are combined in a provisional study. Installed valve identity, flow calibration, exact hose connections and cover baffle remain unverified.

steps.title: A replaceable cover connection
steps.text: The valve inserts into a separate grommet. The manual calls for checking that rubber mounting piece for deterioration.

steps.title: Pressure and spring force
steps.text: The factory cutaway shows a plunger and spring. Pressure forces move the plunger relative to the metering opening. This model does not simulate valve travel or airflow.

steps.title: Metering opening
steps.text: The orifice washer surrounds the tapered plunger. Its clearance influences the available flow area; the modeled dimensions are illustrative.

steps.title: Angled connections
steps.text: The Standard V219 reference has two angled hose connectors. The installed truck routing and unused-outlet closure remain to be established.

troubleshooting.title: Grommet condition
troubleshooting.text: The factory service procedure identifies deterioration of the mounting grommet as an inspection item.

troubleshooting.title: Check the complete path
troubleshooting.text: The factory system diagram includes a clean-air closure hose as well as the metered return path. Missing or disconnected plumbing cannot be assessed from the valve alone.

crankcase-ventilation.summary: Crankcase ventilation returns blow-by gases to the intake. A spring-loaded plunger meters flow, and a separate grommet locates the valve in the cover.
crankcase-ventilation.limits: Factory mechanism and replacement-photo exterior are combined in a provisional study. Installed valve identity, flow calibration, exact hose connections and cover baffle remain unverified.

steps.title: A replaceable cover connection
steps.text: The valve inserts into a separate grommet. The manual calls for checking that rubber mounting piece for deterioration.

steps.title: Pressure and spring force
steps.text: The factory cutaway shows a plunger and spring. Pressure forces move the plunger relative to the metering opening. This model does not simulate valve travel or airflow.

steps.text: The orifice washer surrounds the tapered plunger. Its clearance influences the available flow area; the modeled dimensions are illustrative.

steps.text: The Standard V219 reference has two angled hose connectors. The installed truck routing and unused-outlet closure remain to be established.

troubleshooting.title: Grommet condition
troubleshooting.text: The factory service procedure identifies deterioration of the mounting grommet as an inspection item.

troubleshooting.text: The factory system diagram includes a clean-air closure hose as well as the metered return path. Missing or disconnected plumbing cannot be assessed from the valve alone.

egr.summary: The EGR system meters exhaust into the intake. The PCM commands vacuum through a separate regulator and receives valve-position feedback from the EVP sensor.
egr.limits: Valve and sensor geometry are provisional studies. The exhaust tube, regulator, vacuum hoses, wiring and actual calibration remain unfinished. The static model does not simulate flow, temperature or sensor voltage.

steps.title: Meter exhaust
steps.text: Vacuum acting across the diaphragm lifts the guided pintle against a closing spring. The resulting seat opening admits exhaust to the intake outlet.

steps.title: Measure position
steps.text: The sensor follows valve movement. Its three-terminal potentiometer provides feedback independently of the vacuum solenoid command. Internal contact geometry here is illustrative.

steps.title: Seal the intake connection
steps.text: Two mounting bolts clamp the valve outlet and gasket against the plenum interface. Gasket variant and production mounting dimensions remain unresolved.

troubleshooting.title: Command and feedback are separate
troubleshooting.text: The EVTM shows C180 for the vacuum-control solenoid and C182 for position feedback. A feedback fault does not by itself identify a failed vacuum solenoid or blocked exhaust passage.

troubleshooting.title: Position is not a flow measurement
troubleshooting.text: EVP reports valve position. Open passages and a pressure difference are also necessary for gas flow, so valve movement alone does not prove the exhaust path is clear.

egr-valve-assembly.summary: Inspect the body passage, guided pintle, flexible diaphragm and spring separately.
egr-valve-assembly.limits: A static teaching section based on factory architecture and replacement photographs. Dimensions, seat contour and attachment details remain provisional.

steps.title: Pressure moves the diaphragm
steps.text: The pressure difference between the vacuum chamber and vented lower housing acts across the diaphragm.

steps.title: The pintle opens a metering area
steps.text: The stem transfers diaphragm movement to the pintle. Lifting off its seat creates an opening between inlet and outlet.

steps.title: The spring closes the valve
steps.text: The closing spring biases the assembly toward the seated position as the vacuum command decreases.

egr-position-sensor.summary: A follower transfers EGR movement to a three-terminal position-sensing circuit.
egr-position-sensor.limits: The EVTM verifies the potentiometer circuit. The modeled linear track, collector, wiper and internal supports are illustrative, with no teardown or resistance calibration.

steps.title: Follow mechanical movement
steps.text: The follower touches the valve stem; the small spring represents the force that keeps contact.

steps.title: Produce electrical feedback
steps.text: The wiper samples a position along a resistance. The illustrated collector and track express the EVTM potentiometer circuit, not a verified production contact layout.

steps.title: Return a signal to the PCM
steps.text: EVTM23-4 identifies signal circuit352 BR/LG to PCM27, reference351 BR/W to PCM26 and return359 GY/R to PCM46. Physical connector cavity mapping is still unfinished.

egr-exhaust-line.summary: A separate metal tube connects the rear exhaust manifold to the EGR valve. The valve meters this exhaust into the intake; the tube itself does not control flow.
egr-exhaust-line.limits: Replacement application and outside diameter are sourced. Bend coordinates, wall thickness, coupling dimensions, thread forms and sealing seats remain provisional. The protective sleeve is shown as a smooth shell, not verified braid construction.

steps.title: Follow the exhaust passage
steps.text: The hollow manifold fitting, tube and valve inlet form the exhaust route. Isolate the tube to inspect its two ends.

steps.title: Inspect the connections
steps.text: The valve-end union nut surrounds the tube end and valve inlet. Smooth thread envelopes illustrate assembly relationships; they do not specify a replacement thread or repair dimension.

steps.title: Separate the protective covering
steps.text: Explode the sleeve away from the tube to distinguish the covering from the exhaust passage. Its material and thermal performance have not been established.

troubleshooting.title: Inspect for leakage or blockage
troubleshooting.text: A leaking joint, damaged tube or obstructed passage can affect EGR delivery. Inspect only after the exhaust has cooled, and use the factory diagnostic procedure to distinguish passage faults from vacuum-command and valve faults. A fault code alone does not identify a failed tube.

egr-vacuum-regulator.summary: The PCM controls the vacuum delivered to the EGR diaphragm through an electromagnetic regulator. Its lower port receives manifold vacuum; its upper port supplies the EGR valve.
egr-vacuum-regulator.limits: Exterior reconstruction only. Internal solenoid and valve parts, hose routing, mounting hardware, dimensions and calibrated response remain unfinished. Terminal functions are known electrically, but physical cavity assignments are not verified.

steps.title: Separate command from feedback
steps.text: The two-terminal regulator receives a PCM command; the separate EVP sensor reports EGR position. They have different jobs and separate connectors.

steps.title: Follow the two vacuum ports
steps.text: Ford labels the lower nipple as vacuum source and the upper nipple as the connection to the EGR valve. Increased command duty cycle increases the described output vacuum.

troubleshooting.title: Check the circuit and vacuum supply separately
troubleshooting.text: An electrical circuit fault, missing source vacuum, damaged hose or valve fault can each prevent normal EGR operation. Use the applicable factory pinpoint tests to distinguish these causes; do not diagnose the solenoid from a code alone.

egr-vacuum-lines.summary: The controlled-vacuum hose connects the upper EVR output port to the EGR diaphragm chamber. The separate source-vacuum line is still to be modeled.
egr-vacuum-lines.limits: Hose routing, end diameters, rubber construction and retaining hardware are provisional. This is a connected fit study, not a surveyed factory hose.

steps.title: Trace the command to the diaphragm
steps.text: The hose carries the vacuum signal produced by the regulator. The separate EVP sensor measures valve position electrically.

troubleshooting.title: Inspect the hose path
troubleshooting.text: Leaks, disconnections and restrictions can interrupt the vacuum signal even when the regulator circuit works. Follow the applicable factory vacuum tests to distinguish hose and valve faults.
